title: MCP Gateway Registry server addresses permit requests into internal networks
summary: Authenticated users allowed to register or edit servers can choose upstream addresses that make the gateway request internal services and sometimes return responses, potentially exposing metadata credentials.

severity.rationale: Server-registration privileges can cross a network boundary and disclose cloud credentials. This limited privilege prerequisite with sensitive-data exposure warrants action within 72 hours.

affected.note: Affected through 1.34.0 inclusive. The unrelated 1.25.0 management-API fix does not address this SSRF.

exposure: Requires authenticated registration or modification permission. The registry network and attached role determine reachable services and secrets.

params.instructions: Check the deployed mcp-gateway-registry version: 1.0.3 through 1.34.0 require updating to at least 1.35.0. Inspect stored upstream addresses as well as the running version.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 1.35.0 or later. Review and correct stored server addresses, which are not rewritten by the upgrade. Review registration logs; if unexpected activity cannot be ruled out, review attached-role activity and rotate its credentials. Limit registration permissions and outbound access.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the deployed version is at least 1.35.0 and stored upstream addresses have been reviewed and corrected.
Confirm the registration-log and attached-role reviews and any indicated credential replacement are complete.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
